reuse.why: Reuses setNMonthAvg for the averaging actions, getSheetValue/sum-amount cells for last-month spending, and the shared extractTagsFromText for the #fixed tag, instead of re-implementing them.

duplication.why: setZero/avg/last-month actions share one category selection, but copyPreviousMonth re-states the same hidden/template/#fixed exclusion rules inline on getBudgetData rows, so the rule set lives in two places.

placement.why: Selection helper, tag predicate and new action sit in budget/actions.ts with the handler registered in budget/app.ts, following the tree's layering; getBudgetData is widened only to serve copyPreviousMonth's local checks.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps (exclusions, new action, #fixed, include-hidden flag) plus tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: One selection function with a single flag is easy to own; the parallel row-level rule checks in copyPreviousMonth are a drift risk when the next exclusion is added.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth does not use getMonthWideCategories/getMonthWideBudgetCategories and re-checks hidden, group_hidden, has_template and #fixed on getBudgetData rows.

disguised_duplication.where: The exclusion rules are expressed once as SQL WHERE clauses in getMonthWideCategories and again as per-row if-returns (plus extra has_template/group_note columns in getBudgetData) in copyPreviousMonth.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideCategories gains the includeHiddenCategories parameter with a `? = 1 OR (...)` branch in its SQL; copyPreviousMonth bypasses it with its own inline checks.
